solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I am apt to be cheeky

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
apt means relevant, to the point: pertinent

explanation.surface: Someone admits a tendency to be saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I am apt' as I'M PERTINENT; 'to be' simply links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheeky is being rudely bold or impudent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: To succeed, it must follow her in first

explanation.surface: Advice on how one might come next in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must follow' and 'first' only arrange the three words in order; 'To succeed' reads like winning but means coming after as heir.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title or estate is to receive it as an heir.

clue.text: Police constable held up in a state of terror

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the constable's letters wrap round another piece
in a down clue, up means the words in a are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A frightened policeman is detained in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the short phrase from the bottom; 'held' then wraps the policeman's letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, a state of terror.

clue.text: Normality restored in money-making organisation

indicators.note: restored suggests the letters of normality being put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Things return to normal at a financial institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' rearranges NORMALITY; the ROYAL MINT is the body that makes Britain's coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint literally manufactures money, so it is a money-making body.

clue.text: A club with lofty aims

parts.note: reads like an ambitious society, but describes a golf club whose angled face sends the ball high

explanation.surface: An ambitious society with high ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf clubs of this type have lofted faces that lift the ball, so its 'aims' are literally lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry several of these metal-headed clubs, each lofted to send the ball upward.

clue.text: Nobel Prize winner for Nineties engineering

indicators.note: engineering means contriving or constructing, so the letters of nineties are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A prize awarded for engineering work done in the 1990s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineering' rearranges NINETIES; Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein received the Nobel Prize in Physics, making him a laureate.

clue.text: Wagon overturned on eastern trail

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: A wagon tipped over on a trail heading east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' suits a down clue, where reading upward turns the vehicle over; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a mark or track left behind, as in following a trail.

clue.text: In study group he doesn't share the views of others

definitions.text: doesn't share the views of others

indicators.note: In tells us the word he sits inside the study group

parts.note: a class is a group studying together

explanation.surface: A dissenting student within a seminar group.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing a dissenter, so the answer is a verb in the third person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who clashes with others disagrees or conflicts with their opinions.

clue.text: Writer is about to approve a colour

indicators.note: about means around, so the writer goes round the approving word

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to agree is to approve or consent

explanation.surface: An author is on the point of endorsing a particular shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but the two words do separate jobs: one wraps, one starts the agreeing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a bright yellowish-green shade, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Holiday with one's bride, darling Cynthia!

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like darling
Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon, from the goddess Artemis born on Mount Cynthus

explanation.surface: A man exclaims about a holiday with his new wife, addressing her as Cynthia.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynthia looks like the bride's name, but it is a classical name for the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the trip newlyweds take together after the wedding.

clue.text: A period return to, say, Wembley

indicators.note: return means come back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a period can be an era, and A becomes an before a vowel: an era

explanation.surface: Going back to Wembley stadium for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A period' as AN ERA; 'return' reverses it. Wembley is London's national football stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Wembley is an example of a sports stadium or venue, signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Don't forget to come again

definitions.meaning: to remember something, as in bringing it back to mind
to call back or summon to return, read as call again

explanation.surface: A reminder to return another time.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to remember, and also to call someone back to come again.

clue.text: Full complement of vigour

definitions.meaning: as in 'at full ...', having all the people needed

explanation.surface: A complete set of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A team at full strength has its whole complement; strength also means power or vigour.

clue.text: Bird gets morsel — a choice one

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
a bit is a small piece or morsel

explanation.surface: A bird gets a scrap of food, a tasty one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' in the definition refers back to the morsel: a choice morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small, especially tasty piece of food, a choice bite.

clue.text: Flight path for early aircraft

parts.note: a flight is a journey, a trip
a lane is a narrow path or route

explanation.surface: An air route used by pioneering planes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplane, with three stacked wings, was a type of plane from aviation's early years.

clue.text: Benevolence of sort shown by head

parts.note: kind means sort or type
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A display of goodwill from the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a headteacher but means a promontory, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness is warm goodwill toward others, the same as benevolence.

clue.text: Do some fishing, but keep in touch

definitions.meaning: to cast a fishing line into the water
to send someone a brief letter

explanation.surface: Go angling, but stay in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers literally lower a line; the same phrase means write someone a short note.

clue.text: Cat's coat poorly clipped

indicators.note: poorly means badly, so the letters of the phrase are put in bad order

explanation.surface: A cat's fur has been badly trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges CATSCOAT; 'clipped' looks like grooming but is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato in music means notes played short and detached, clipped.

clue.text: Leaves about ten to play around in musical groups

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the leaving word goes round the shuffled number

parts.note: quits means leaves, as in he quits the job

indicators.note: play around suggests messing about with the letters of ten

explanation.surface: Someone departs at ten to fool about in bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb for departing; 'in' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintets are ensembles of five performers, so they are musical groups.

clue.text: Mercy? Not half!

definitions.meaning: clemency shown to a beaten enemy
a fourth part, which is only half of a half

explanation.surface: An exclamation pleading for mercy, answered emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' looks like slang for 'absolutely', but here means a fraction smaller than a half.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter means clemency to a defeated foe, and also a fourth part, less than half.

clue.text: Tramp meets toff — without love they rarely do this

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for love is dropped

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a nob is an upper-class person, a toff

explanation.surface: A vagrant and an aristocrat rarely socialise without affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without love' removes an O from HOBO, giving HOB; 'meets' joins it to NOB. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, something tramps and toffs seldom do together.

clue.text: Sort of clip that's found at the end of a lead

definitions.meaning: a spring clip used to hold papers together

definitions.text: found at the end of a lead
definitions.meaning: a dog breed, walked on a leash

explanation.surface: A clasp attached to the end of a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldog clip is a strong paper clip; a bulldog is a dog that might be on a leash.

clue.text: Marriage makes a nice change after all

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters following the word all
change means alter, so the letters of a nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wedding someone brings a pleasant change after everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marriage makes' is a natural surface phrase, but 'makes' is just the link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance can be a union by marriage, especially between families.

clue.text: Through which Hamlet drove home his point

definitions.text: Through which Hamlet drove home his point

parts.words: Through which Hamlet drove home his point
parts.note: reads like a persuasive argument, but means the tapestry Hamlet stabbed through to kill Polonius hiding behind it

explanation.surface: How Shakespeare's prince made his argument forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove home his point' means literally thrusting his sword through a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a tapestry hanging, the one Polonius hid behind in Hamlet.

clue.text: Terrible, but not initially loud, stream of abuse

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: fearful can mean terrible, as in a fearful mess
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: A dreadful, though at first quiet, torrent of insults.
explanation.walkthrough: FEARFUL loses its first letter F (loud) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long angry telling-off, a torrent of reproach.

clue.text: The latest thing in ties?

parts.note: sounds like fashionable neckwear, but means the last match in a cup competition, where games are called ties

explanation.surface: Asking about the newest fashion in neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, cup matches are called ties; the last of them is the cup's deciding match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup final is the concluding tie in a knockout tournament, the last one played.

clue.text: National tax

definitions.meaning: a native of one nation, here Scotland
an old word for a levy

explanation.surface: A tax imposed across the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a national of Scotland; scot was also a medieval tax, hence scot-free.

clue.text: Singer gets awkward note right

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy, so the letters of note are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vocalist hits an off note but gets it right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like the musical item a singer hits, but here it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male vocalist with a high voice, a type of singer.

clue.text: Lots are involved in education

indicators.note: involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters of education are mixed up

explanation.surface: Schooling involves a great many things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' suggests many, but means items for sale: lots are auctioned. 'Involved' rearranges EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots at a sale room are put under the hammer, sold by bidding.

clue.text: Let Jack be seen to supply a military presence

definitions.meaning: to display the Union Jack, the British national banner
to send armed forces to make one's power felt

explanation.surface: Display the Union Jack to signal armed strength abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaying a flag literally shows it; idiomatically the phrase means asserting power by military presence.
